purpose: Fresh grayscale overworld concept; not based on prior project spikes
prompt: Create a grayscale pixel-art concept sheet for a top-down overworld in a tiny 128×64 monochrome handheld game. This is a fresh art direction; do not imitate any existing game, reference sheet, or provided asset. Canvas: wide landscape 2:1. Exact layout: a clean 2-column × 2-row contact sheet of four equally sized landscape panels, each panel exactly 2:1, divided only by a narrow blank white gutter. No titles, no labels, no UI, no borders around panels. Strict orthographic top-down JRPG map view, not isometric and no horizon. Draw the scenery as chunky pixel art designed to reduce clearly to a 128×64 viewport built on a 16×16 tile grid. Keep a clear, walkable route through each panel and leave an open 16×16 tile patch at screen center for a real 16×16 player sprite to be composited later. Every scene must have large readable shapes and distinct landmarks at small scale. Upper-left: a cave passage with irregular rock walls, a pool, a few bright crystal clusters and a readable path. Upper-right: a forest trail winding between broad tree canopies, ferns, logs and a small clearing. Lower-left: a rural village lane with two compact cottages, a fence, vegetable beds and a well. Lower-right: a compact city street with close-set storefronts, sidewalk blocks, street lamps and a small plaza. Work in grayscale from white through middle grays to black so the same scene can be exported into several different 1-bit treatments. Use broad tonal clusters and solid pixel edges. Do not bake dithering, halftone, grain, crosshatching or tiny speckled texture into the source; those will be compared separately during conversion. Keep enough clean white ground that a player sprite remains legible.
